\chapter{Forms and Introductions}
\label{ch:hi-forms-and-introductions}
\hlchaptermodality{120}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can sign a form, talk about an identity card, introduce myself, and say it was nice to meet someone.}

Complete HI-C120-milkar: from the form to the handshake.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[hastākṣar]{\hi{हस्ताक्षर} (hastākṣar) — a signature}

\label{lesson:HI-C120-hastakshar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for married, then the Hindi for a birthday.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{हस्ताक्षर}}
\textbf{\hi{हस्ताक्षर}} (\emph{hastākṣar}) — \textquotedblleft{}a signature\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}hand-letters\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{हाथ}} and this word's \textbf{\hi{हस्त}-} are the same old word for hand. \textbf{\hi{यहाँ} \hi{हस्ताक्षर} \hi{कीजिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}please sign here\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A signature, built on the word for hand.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hastākṣar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hastākṣar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{yahā̃ hastākṣar kījie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for married, then the Hindi for a birthday, then say \emph{hastākṣar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{हस्ताक्षर} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A signature\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pahcān]{\hi{पहचान} (pahcān) — identity; recognition}

\label{lesson:HI-C120-pahchan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a birthday, then the Hindi for a signature.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{पहचान}}
\textbf{\hi{पहचान}} (\emph{pahcān}) — \textquotedblleft{}identity\textquotedblright{}, and \textquotedblleft{}recognition\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{पहचान} \hi{पत्र}} — \textquotedblleft{}an identity card\textquotedblright{}. The same word is the knowing-again of a familiar face.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
What a form asks you to prove.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pahcān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pahcān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{pahcān patra}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a birthday, then the Hindi for a signature, then say \emph{pahcān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{पहचान} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Identity; recognition\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[paricay]{\hi{परिचय} (paricay) — an introduction}

\label{lesson:HI-C120-parichay}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for a signature, then the Hindi for identity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{परिचय}}
\textbf{\hi{परिचय}} (\emph{paricay}) — \textquotedblleft{}an introduction\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{अपना} \hi{परिचय} \hi{दीजिए}} — \textquotedblleft{}please introduce yourself\textquotedblright{}, with the \textbf{\hi{अपना}} you know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A request to hear who someone is.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paricay}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paricay}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{apnā paricay dījie}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for a signature, then the Hindi for identity, then say \emph{paricay} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{परिचय} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An introduction\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[insān]{\hi{इंसान} (insān) — a human being, a person}

\label{lesson:HI-C120-insan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for identity, then the Hindi for an introduction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{इंसान}}
\textbf{\hi{इंसान}} (\emph{insān}) — \textquotedblleft{}a human being, a person\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\hi{अच्छा} \hi{इंसान}} — \textquotedblleft{}a good person\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\hi{अच्छा}}. \textbf{\hi{आदमी}} is a man; \textbf{\hi{इंसान}} is anyone.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A word for anyone at all.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{insān}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{insān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{acchā insān}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for identity, then the Hindi for an introduction, then say \emph{insān} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{इंसान} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A human being, a person\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[milkar acchā lagā]{\hi{मिलकर} \hi{अच्छा} \hi{लगा} (milkar acchā lagā) — nice to meet you}

\label{lesson:HI-C120-milkar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for an introduction, then the Hindi for a person.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{मिलकर} \hi{अच्छा} \hi{लगा}}
\textbf{\hi{मिलकर} \hi{अच्छा} \hi{लगा}} (\emph{milkar acchā lagā}) — \textquotedblleft{}nice to meet you\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}having met, it felt good\textquotedblright{}.

It is the everyday cousin of \textbf{\hi{आपसे} \hi{मिलकर} \hi{ख़ुशी} \hi{हुई}}, built on the same \textbf{\hi{मिलना}}, \textquotedblleft{}to meet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A signature, an identity, an introduction, a person, and the goodbye after meeting.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{milkar acchā lagā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{milkar acchā lagā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{milkar acchā lagā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Hindi for an introduction, then the Hindi for a person, then say \emph{milkar acchā lagā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{मिलकर} \hi{अच्छा} \hi{लगा} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Nice to meet you\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
